Krown Bowling on paper

Write the numbers 1 to 10 or name them aloud. Start each puzzle with all ten pins standing. Choose an aim twice. On each roll, cross out or remove only pins from that aim’s row that are still standing. A pin that is already down cannot fall again.

Pins each aim can reach
AimPins
Left2, 4, 7, 8
Center1, 2, 3, 5
Right3, 6, 9, 10

Try the same aim twice

Roll Center twice. How many pins does the second roll knock down? Which pins are still standing?

Check your answer

None fall on roll two. Pins 4, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10 are still standing because Center already knocked down every pin it could reach.

Leave only pins 1 and 5

Start a fresh rack. Can you leave exactly pins 1 and 5 standing after two rolls? Does the order matter?

Check your aim

Left and Right leave only 1 and 5. The two aims reach different pins, so either order works. Center would hit both pins you want to leave standing.

Find your best two rolls

Start fresh again. What is the most pins you can knock down in two rolls? Find every pair of aims that does it, counting each pair once.

Check the pairs

Eight pins. Left and Right share no pins, so each knocks down four. Center and Right share pin 3; together they knock down seven. Left and Center share pin 2; together they also knock down seven. Using the same aim twice knocks down four.
